tagline: The science of water in forests — research and knowledge, made accessible.
meta_description: ForestHydrology.com is a multilingual science outlet on forest hydrology: research on the water cycle in forests and its effects on climate, water management, and ecosystems.
home_hero_title: Forest hydrology — from headwater to outlet
home_hero_subtitle: We publish peer-informed knowledge on how forests store, purify, and release water — written for scientists and for anyone who wants to understand forests as part of the water cycle.
home_mission_text: Forests regulate water flow, protect soils from erosion, filter pollutants, and buffer the effects of floods and droughts. Understanding these processes is essential for water management, forestry, and climate adaptation.
topic_interception_text: How tree canopies, litter, and forest soils capture and release rainfall.
topic_quality_text: The role of streamside forests in filtering pollutants and protecting waterways.
topic_snow_text: How forest cover affects snow accumulation and melt in mountain catchments.
topic_climate_text: Feedbacks between forest water cycling and the global climate system.

about_intro: ForestHydrology.com is an independent, multilingual science and education outlet dedicated to forest hydrology — the study of how forests shape the movement of water through nature.
about_body: Our goal is to combine sound scientific knowledge with accessible writing. We publish articles grounded in the scientific literature, explain the research methods used in forest hydrology, and describe why forests are a critical part of catchment water management. The site is developed in the open — its source code is public, and content is translated into four languages to reach a wider, international readership.
about_value_1_text: Articles reference peer-reviewed scientific literature and clearly separate facts from interpretation.
about_value_2_text: We translate complex hydrological concepts into language non-specialists can follow.
about_value_3_text: The site is an open-source project, and content is published in four languages.
